definitions.explanation: The art of arranging flowers in a vase or container. A formal, literary synonym for ikebana (生け花). Used particularly in written and academic contexts.

examples.japanese: {挿花|そうか}の{教室|きょうしつ}に{通|かよ}っている。
examples.english: I attend a flower arrangement class.

examples.japanese: {床|とこ}の{間|ま}に{挿花|そうか}が{飾|かざ}ってあった。
examples.english: A flower arrangement was displayed in the tokonoma alcove.

examples.japanese: {挿花|そうか}は{日本|にほん}の{伝統的|でんとうてき}な{芸術|げいじゅつ}のひとつとして{世界|せかい}に{知|し}られている。
examples.english: Flower arrangement is known worldwide as one of Japan's traditional arts.

notes:
Composed of {挿|そう} (to insert) + {花|か} (flower). A literary and formal term for flower arrangement. In everyday speech and most contexts, {生|い}け{花|ばな} or {華道|かどう} are more commonly used.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {挿花|そうか}の{稽古|けいこ}: flower arrangement practice
- {挿花|そうか}を{習|なら}う: to learn flower arrangement
- {挿花|そうか}の{作品|さくひん}: a flower arrangement work

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {生|い}け{花|ばな}: ikebana -- the most common everyday term for Japanese flower arrangement
- {華道|かどう}: the way of flowers -- emphasizes it as a traditional art or discipline
- {花道|かどう}: alternate writing of the same term (less common)
- {投|な}げ{入|い}れ: nageire -- a specific casual style of flower arrangement
